subject: Clarify hosted rate card: Chat Completions vs Responses vs legacy endpoint units
messages:
From: Eliot Summers <eliot@brightlane.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@brightlane.ai
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted rate card: units mapping question

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement is working through our cloud costs and we need a clear, line-by-line explanation of how Redwood maps billing units for your hosted API. Specifically:

- How do Chat Completions, Responses, and the older/legacy endpoints map to tokens or billing units?
- Are system + assistant + user tokens counted the same way across endpoints?
- Is streaming billed differently than non-streaming responses?
- What's the baseline hosted price per unit and how do volume discounts kick in (we expect ~10M tokens/month initially)?

Can you send a short example calculation (2 prompts, 1 response, 1 streaming token scenario) so procurement can place into our cost model? If possible, include a sample invoice row we can show our finance team.

Appreciate the clarity — Eliot
Eliot Summers
Head of Platform
BrightLane AI

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Eliot Summers <eliot@brightlane.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, procurement@brightlane.ai
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2026 10:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted rate card: units mapping question

Hi Eliot — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together a concise mapping and an example invoice row (attached). Key points up top:

1) Unit model summary
- Chat Completions endpoint: billed by "generation tokens" + "input tokens" where assistant outputs are counted per-token; system/user/assistant all count as tokens in the same bucket.
- Responses endpoint (newer consolidated API): bills per "response unit" which maps to tokens but can include structured outputs and function-call payloads; economics are equivalent to Chat Completions for plain text but can differ for heavy function outputs.
- Legacy endpoints: older route names (v0/chat, v0/completions) are still supported; they map 1:1 to either Chat Completions or Responses unit logic depending on call shape.

2) Streaming vs non-streaming
- Streaming: we charge on tokens emitted (same per-token rate). There is no separate streaming surcharge. However, streaming encourages lower latency and can change effective token usage (clients often send shorter prompts).

3) Example calculations (attached CSV, excerpt below)
- Scenario A (Chat Completions): 2 prompts (each 150 tokens) + assistant reply 600 tokens = 900 tokens total billed.
- Scenario B (Responses endpoint with function-output): input 300 tokens, response 800 tokens including function-json output = 1100 response-units billed (mapped to tokens with slight rounding).

4) Baseline pricing & discount bands (hosted API)
- Published base: $0.0008 per token-equivalent (baseline public rate).
- Discount bands by committed monthly volume: 0-1M tokens = list; 1M-10M = 10% off; 10M-50M = 20% off; 50M+ = custom.
- For your expected ~10M tokens/month we typically start at the 10% band and offer an introductory 5% additional commercial discount for first 3 months on new enterprise deals.

5) Sample invoice row (CSV attached):
- Date, Product, Endpoint, Units, Unit price, Extended
- 2026-11-01, hosted-inference, responses, 1,000,000, $0.00072, $720

I've attached ratecard_hosted_v2.pdf with the official table and example-invoice.csv that shows the calculation cells. Karthik — can you add a brief note below about how legacy endpoints are remapped for customers migrating from our old SDKs? Vivek — FYI on the introductory commercial discount.

Next step: Happy to jump on a 30m call with your procurement & finance to walk the invoice example through. Are you available Wed 12/1 or Thu 12/2?

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0191

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Eliot Summers <eliot@brightlane.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, procurement@brightlane.ai
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2026 13:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted rate card: units mapping question

Quick technical add:
- Legacy endpoints: when customers call legacy completion endpoints with the same message-structure as chat, our billing pipeline tags the call and maps tokens to the Chat Completions pricing model. There is no double-charge or hidden conversion fee — just a mapping layer in the metering pipeline.
- Responses endpoint: supports structured outputs and function-call payloads; for large JSON function outputs we compute token-equivalent by tokenizing the UTF-8 payload same as assistant text. In practice that means heavy-function outputs will increase your billed tokens proportionally.
- Example edge case: if you use streaming + partial function-calls (streamed JSON pieces) we bill per emitted token chunk.

If BrightLane plans to migrate from an older SDK, we can provide a small test harness that runs 1K sample calls and outputs the expected monthly token delta so procurement can model it.

-Karthik
Principal Product Manager, Pricing & Packaging
Redwood Inference
